candidate_spec.high_level_variant: Ego follows its route into a mildly denser mixed-traffic area where a crossing vehicle from the side approaches and is detected and predicted, but ego continues forward and collides laterally without braking while planning still outputs unblocked waypoints and vehicle_cmd stays all zero.
candidate_spec.mutation_intent: Shift the primary interacting actor to approach from a lateral direction while keeping the ego moving and preserving active perception/prediction and unblocked planning outputs alongside a zeroed vehicle_cmd stream. The lateral configuration explores whether the same command–status mismatch and unexplained collision arise when the nearby actor is not purely longitudinal, without changing the core root-cause pattern.
pre_execution_validation_rules: Verify that actor_index 3’s adjusted pose and speed create a plausible lateral or diagonal path that intersects the ego lane within the simulation horizon, so that a potential side collision region exists.
Confirm that the mission spawn and destination offsets still place ego on a continuous roadway path without invalid or off-road starts/ends.
Ensure perception and prediction topics are active and configured to detect and track vehicles approaching from the sides, not just purely longitudinal traffic.
Check planning still produces full final_waypoints with no preconfigured blocked segments or emergency-stop logic specific to cross-traffic in this map region.
Confirm the controller and simulator configuration still allow vehicle_status to report ego motion even when vehicle_cmd fields may remain zero.
post_execution_validation_rules: Confirm oracle collision logs a collision between ego and a non-ego vehicle (preferably actor_index 3) near the end of the run.
Verify ego velocity remains nonzero leading up to the collision and there is no significant increase in brake_cmd before impact.

Check that perception/prediction topics report the laterally approaching vehicle with positions and predicted trajectories that intersect or closely approach the ego’s path in the seconds before the collision.
Ensure final_waypoints remain present, with consistent counts and no blocked flags, throughout the pre-collision window, indicating planning did not explicitly mark the path as obstructed.
Validate that vehicle_cmd accel_cmd, brake_cmd, steer_cmd, and target_speed stay effectively at zero while vehicle_status shows ongoing motion, reproducing the command–status mismatch.
Inspect any planner summary metrics (e.g., closest-object-distance) to verify that they do not trigger a stop or blocked-plan condition even as the lateral actor nears the ego.
uncertainty: Changing the main interacting actor to a lateral vehicle may influence how perception and prediction represent the scene, so it remains uncertain whether the same misalignment between their outputs and planning/control will occur.

The underlying cause of the zero vehicle_cmd despite ego motion is still ambiguous; this variant tests whether the phenomenon generalizes to cross-traffic, but does not identify which module is responsible if the pattern repeats.

note: Generated candidate scenario JSON for local DriveFuzz execution. It has not been executed in CARLA/Autoware.
